newsitem.title: USA: U.S. actor's court hearing moved by caterpillar.
newsitem.headline: U.S. actor's court hearing moved by caterpillar.

text.p: A court appearance for actor Woody Harrelson on marijuana possession charges has been run out of town by the wooly bear caterpillar.

The Lee County Circuit Court clerk's office said on Wednesday Harrelson's case, scheduled to be heard on Friday, had been moved to Booneville, Kentucky, and reset for Oct. 30 because Beattyville is in the throes of its annual "Wooly Worm Festival."

Throngs gathering for the annual autumn fete, which celebrates the caterpillar's legendary ability to forecast the coming winter weather by the size and colour of its coat, will force the court house to shut down, the clerk's office said.

Harrelson was charged with marijuana possession last June after he planted four industrial hemp seeds on a plot of land he owns in a move designed to challenge the state's law against growing the plant.

Hemp was the leading farm crop in Kentucky from the early 18th century until the 1930s. Harrelson contends it should be legalised because the industrial variety contains little of the psychoactive ingredient in marijuana and the state law errs in failing to make a distinction between the two plants.
His lawyer, R. Burl McCoy of Lexington, said he has filed a request for a dismissal of the charges. That issue will be decided at the Oct. 30 hearing in Booneville.

McCoy told Reuters the request was part of a move to establish a record in the case and he did not expect the judge to grant it. He said Harrelson planned to continue his challenge of the law, taking it to the state's supreme court if necessary.
Harrelson became known as clueless barkeeper Woody on the television sitcom "Cheers." He has also featured in films such as "White Men Can't Jump" and "Indecent Proposal."
